2026-11-09.lens: The Great Mental Models, Vol. 1 (Parrish): use second-order thinking. For each story, ask 'and then what?' to see the consequences that follow the obvious first effect.

items.title: US land blockade on Iran begins as Trump plays down new strikes
items.why: Washington says its blockade of Iran's land supply routes is now in force, while Trump calls fresh strikes highly unlikely if talks on the nuclear programme and reopening Hormuz move forward; Tehran threatens heavy retaliation if attacked. For India, how this ends decides oil import costs, the rupee and the safety of Gulf shipping lanes and diaspora remittances.
items.question: Using second-order thinking: if the land blockade squeezes Iran harder, what is the likely second move by Tehran around Hormuz, and how would that reach India's fuel prices and trade?

items.title: India's inflation climbs as forex reserves slip ahead of key data
items.why: Retail inflation hit a 2026 high of 5.54% in September, driven by food, and October's figure lands on 12 November; reserves have fallen for two weeks to about $717 billion as the RBI sells dollars to support the rupee. This sets up a squeeze between defending the currency and keeping rates supportive of growth.
items.question: Applying the 'map is not the territory' model: what does a single headline CPI number hide about how inflation is felt differently by urban and rural households?

items.title: Nvidia board probes Jensen Huang over alleged China spy link
items.why: Independent directors are investigating the CEO after he admitted a relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence, whose employer became a multibillion-dollar Nvidia buyer; Congress wants testimony on 18 November. It shows how the world's most important AI supplier is now a national-security object, which can tighten chip export rules that affect AI builders everywhere, including India.
items.question: Using inversion: what would have to be true for this episode to end up strengthening Nvidia's position rather than weakening it?

items.title: IT drags Indian markets while pharma hits a record
items.why: Sensex and Nifty traded slightly lower on Monday as HCLTech and Infosys led an IT decline, while the pharma index touched a record high and softer crude eased inflation worries. The split shows investors repricing India's services exporters in an AI era while rewarding sectors seen as defensive.
items.question: Through the circle-of-competence lens: which part of the AI threat to Indian IT services do investors truly understand, and where are they pricing fear rather than knowledge?
